page: Microsoft Azure D16ads_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dadv6 series, powered by AMD EPYC 9V74 processors. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The compute layer features hardware acceleration support including AVX-512 extensions (F, VNNI, and BF16) alongside SHA and AES cryptographic instructions. The instance is provisioned with 64 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation ratio.

Storage configuration includes a dedicated local 944 GB NVMe SSD for high-throughput ephemeral caching and scratch space, while remote premium storage is also supported. Benchmark evaluations demonstrate strong single-thread execution, placing the instance in the top 25% of evaluated systems for single-core stress-ng tests and Geekbench single-core scores (1992.0). Multi-threaded compute performance remains balanced across PassMark CPU (26254.79) and multi-core stress-ng tests. However, memory bandwidth on large uncached read blocks sits in the lower 25% quartile at 37.84 GB/sec, representing a performance bottleneck for data-streaming pipelines.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D16ads_v6 yields balanced compute density by pairing modern Zen-generation CPU cores with onboard fast NVMe storage, eliminating external disk costs for intermediate workloads. It is well matched for mid-tier relational and in-memory databases, continuous integration build servers, backend application clusters, and lightweight CPU-based machine learning inference where high single-threaded performance and low-latency scratch space are required.
description: Microsoft Azure D16ads_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine equipped with 16 dedicated vCPUs and 64 GB of RAM, running on an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor at 3.7 GHz under Microsoft Hyper-V. The system incorporates modern instruction sets such as AVX-512 and includes 944 GB of direct-attached local NVMe SSD storage. Benchmark results show strong single-core CPU throughput in Geekbench and stress-ng tests, balanced multi-core metrics, and standard memory bandwidth, though uncached large-block memory read bandwidth remains comparatively low. With an even 1:4 core-to-memory ratio and bundled local NVMe storage, this configuration delivers reliable resource density for web application clusters, container hosting, relational databases, software build nodes, and small-model inference tasks.
